podcast.title: Band Formation and Early Lineup
podcast.body: Formed by Roy Orbison and a group of friends in his teens, the band was named after their small town of Wink. It had various lineups before settling on a two-guitar, bass, drums, and electric mandolin configuration with Orbison, Billy Pat Ellis, Jack Caneeley, Johnny Wilson, and James Morrow. "In his teens he and a group of his friends formed a country in western band, the Wink Westerners, named after the small town they lived in. That band had various lineups but it eventually settled into a two guitar, bass, drums and electric mandolin lineup of Orbison, Billy Pat Ellis, Jack Caneeley, Johnny Wilson and James Morrow."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Local Radio Show and Backing Slim Whitman
podcast.body: While Roy Orbison was still in school, The Wink Westerners secured their own weekly radio show. Their local popularity led to them being chosen as the backing group for country star Slim Whitman when he came to town. "While Orbison was still in school the band got their own radio show one day a week and became big enough that when the country star Slim Whitman came to town they were chosen as his backing group."

podcast.title: Renamed The Teen Kings
podcast.body: Following Roy Orbison's transformative experience with rock and roll on New Year's Eve 1954, The Wink Westerners were quickly renamed The Teen Kings. "The wink westerners were quickly renamed the team Kings."

podcast.title: Roy Orbison's First Group
podcast.body: This was Roy Orbison's initial musical group, where he started his career as a rocker-billy singer. "Roy Orbison had started out as a rocker-billy singer, with a group called The Wing Westerners."
